raw_case_text:
On October 29th 2005, a 56-year-old German tourist living in Haiti, with a history of heavy alcohol use and 2 malaria infections treated with chloroquine, developed symptoms of fever, headache, nausea, and diarrhea. On November 3rd he visited a local hospital in Cotes des Arcadins and was diagnosed with P. falciparum infection by peripheral blood smear. The patient was treated with chloroquine and doxycycline the same day but developed altered mental status and was hospitalized. Despite falling parasite counts, the patient's neurological condition continued to worsen and he was mechanically ventilated. Seizures, bloody stools, hematemesis, and decreased urinary output were also documented. Due to his worsening condition, he was transferred to a hospital in Miami the following day, November 4th.  At the time of hospital admission in Miami, the patient had thrombocytopenia, diffuse intravascular coagulation, electrolyte imbalance, and acute renal failure. Blood smears showed few malaria parasites, but treatment with antimalarial agents was continued.  Bronchoalveolar lavage was positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomas aeruginosa, and yeast forms.
Blood culture on November 4th was positive for C.  perfringens. Vancomycin, amphotericin, piperacillin, phenytoin, lorazepam, and hydrocortisone were added to the treatment regimen. On November 5th blood culture revealed Candida tropicalis. An encephalitis panel was also negative. The patient continued to decline clinically and he expired on November 7th, 10 days after symptom onset.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 56-year-old male presenting with fever, headache, nausea, diarrhea, followed by progressive altered mental status, seizures, and gastrointestinal hemorrhage.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 56-year-old male tourist living in Haiti developed fever, headache, nausea, and diarrhea on October 29, 2005. On November 3, he presented to a local hospital in Haiti and was prescribed antimicrobial therapy. However, he developed acute altered mental status and was hospitalized and intubated for mechanical ventilation. He developed generalized seizures, hematemesis, melena/hematochezia, and oliguria, prompting emergency air medical evacuation to Miami on November 4.
subjective.past_medical_history: German tourist residing in Haiti. History of heavy alcohol use and two prior malaria infections treated with chloroquine. Pre-transfer medications: chloroquine and doxycycline initiated on November 3.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, headache, nausea, diarrhea, hematemesis, bloody stools, seizures, and altered sensorium. Medications: chloroquine, doxycycline. Allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Critically ill, comatose/altered mental status on mechanical ventilation. Hemodynamically unstable, oliguria/anuria. Abdomen: distended with signs of gastrointestinal bleeding (hematochezia and hematemesis via gastric tube). Skin: petechiae/purpura.
objective.routine_investigations: Thrombocytopenia, diffuse intravascular coagulation (DIC), severe electrolyte imbalances, and acute renal failure. Serial peripheral blood smears performed. Encephalitis panel: negative. Blood cultures: positive for Clostridium perfringens on November 4; repeat blood culture positive for Candida tropicalis on November 5. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) culture: positive for Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and yeast forms.
objective.advanced_workup: Diagnostic bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and lumbar puncture with viral/encephalitis panel.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria complicated by cerebral malaria, multiorgan dysfunction syndrome (DIC, acute renal failure, respiratory failure), gastrointestinal hemorrhage, Clostridium perfringens bacteremia, Candida tropicalis fungemia, and polymicrobial ventilator-associated pneumonia.
Diagnostic confirmation: Initial peripheral blood smear in Haiti demonstrating Plasmodium falciparum; subsequent blood smears in Miami demonstrating low-level intraerythrocytic parasites; blood cultures confirming Clostridium perfringens bacteremia and Candida tropicalis fungemia; BAL cultures yielding K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, and P. aeruginosa.
Treatment & Outcome: Managed with mechanical ventilation, broad-spectrum antimicrobial and antifungal therapy including IV vancomycin, amphotericin, piperacillin, continued antimalarials, anticonvulsant therapy with phenytoin and lorazepam, and IV hydrocortisone. Despite intensive supportive care, multiorgan failure progressed and the patient died on November 7 (day 10 of illness).
